key_idea: Insert players in decreasing skill order, each into the contest that currently maximizes their payoff p_j/(t_j+s); later (weaker) arrivals can never make an earlier player want to deviate.
sketch: Sort by skill descending; for each player pick contest minimizing (t_j+s)/p_j, compared exactly by cross-multiplication in 64-bit (values < 2e18). Proof: when a player of skill s joins i, (t_i+s)/p_i <= (t_j+s)/p_j for all j; any earlier member of i has s' >= s so their deviation value (t_j+s')/p_j is even larger, and members of other contests only see i get worse. O(n*m) = 2e7. Pitfalls: empty contests are legal (print 0), avoid floating point. Multiple answers are accepted so the token checker reports WRONG on the samples; samples_passed is based on my own validator, which checked the Nash condition with exact fractions on 400 random small cases.
